faqs.q: Is SWP better than a fixed deposit for monthly income?
faqs.a: It depends on what you need. An SWP can be more tax-efficient because only the gain in each withdrawal is taxed, while all FD interest is taxed at your slab rate. But mutual fund returns are not guaranteed, so your balance can fall in a bad market, unlike an FD's fixed interest.

faqs.q: Can I stop or change my SWP at any time?
faqs.a: Yes. Fund houses let you pause, stop or change the amount and frequency of an SWP through their website, app or your distributor. Changes usually need a few working days' notice before the next withdrawal date.

faqs.q: Is money withdrawn through SWP taxable?
faqs.a: Partly. Each SWP withdrawal is a redemption of units, so only the gain in it is taxed as capital gains; the part that is your original investment is not taxed. The rate depends on the type of fund and how long you held the units, so check the current rules before you start.

faqs.q: How much should I withdraw through SWP so my money lasts?
faqs.a: Keep your yearly withdrawals below what the fund can reasonably earn over the long term, so the balance is not eaten up. Withdrawing a small percentage of your corpus each year from a hybrid or debt-oriented fund gives steadier income than a large withdrawal from a volatile fund.
